Let me look at the project structure. The task: pytest 6 dynamically adding xfail marker via request.node.add_marker no longer ignores failure. Find cause and minimal fix in source.

This is pytest repo at an old commit (6.0.0rc0 era). The known fix: in `_pytest/skipping.py`, the xfail evaluation. In pytest 6, markers were changed to be stored in `Node.own_markers` and `Node.iter_markers`. The issue: `add_marker` adds to `own_markers`, but the skipping plugin evaluates xfail via `evaluate_xfail_marks` which uses `item.iter_markers()`... Actually the known pytest issue #7486 "Dynamically adding xfail marker in test no longer ignores failure" — fixed by PR #7492? Let me recall.

The actual cause: In pytest 6, `Skipped`/xfail handling moved to `skipping.py` with `pytest_runtest_makereport` hookwrapper checking `item.iter_markers(name="xfail")`. Hmm, but that should see dynamically added markers.

Actually the real cause: `Node.add_marker` in 6.0 adds marker to `own_markers`, but the xfail evaluation happens in `pytest_runtest_setup`? No — xfail evaluation happens at report time in `pytest_runtest_makereport` via `evaluate_xfail_marks(item)`. Hmm.

Let me recall the actual fix commit: "skipping: fix dynamically adding xfail marker" — the issue was that `evaluate_xfail_marks` was called with `item` but the markers were read from `item.own_markers` directly instead of `iter_markers`? Or the issue was that in 6.0, `add_marker` no longer re-parses... Actually I recall the fix: PR #7492 "Fix dynamic xfail marker" changed `Node.add_marker` to also update... Hmm.

Better to just look at the code. Let me explore the repo.

Actually the real cause per pytest changelog 6.0.1: "#7486: Fix dynamically adding an xfail marker to a test no longer ignores the failure." The fix commit: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/pull/7492? Let me think about what the change was.

In pytest 6.0, `skipping.py`:

```python
@hookimpl(hookwrapper=True)
def pytest_runtest_makereport(item: Item, call):
    outcome = yield
    rep = outcome.get_result()
    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, False)
    ...
```

and in `pytest_runtest_setup`... Actually xfail evaluation: `evaluate_xfail_marks(item)` is called in `pytest_runtest_setup`? No — it's called in `pytest_runtest_makereport`? Let me recall 6.0 code:

```python
def pytest_runtest_setup(item):
    skipped = evaluate_skip_marks(item)
    if skipped:
        raise Skipped(...)
    item._store[xfailed_key] = xfailed = evaluate_xfail_marks(item)
    if xfailed and not item.config.option.runxfail and xfailed.reason:
        ...
```

Hmm, that's setup. Then in makereport:

```python
@hookimpl(hookwrapper=True)
def pytest_runtest_makereport(item, call):
    outcome = yield
    rep = outcome.get_result()
    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, False)
    if item.config.option.runxfail:
        pass
    else:
        if xfailed:
            ...
```

So xfail is evaluated at setup time and stored. If you add the marker dynamically inside the test (during call phase), the stored value from setup is False, so the failure isn't xfailed. In pytest 5, the evaluation happened in makereport directly reading markers at report time.

Wait, but the issue says "In 5.x this treated the failing test like a test marked statically with xfail. With 6.0.0rc0 it raises." So the fix would be to evaluate xfail marks at report time (in makereport) rather than relying on the setup-time stored value. Actually the actual fix in pytest was PR #7492: "skipping: evaluate xfail marks at report time" or something. Let me check the actual 6.0.1 changelog entry: "#7486: Fix a bug where dynamically adding an xfail marker to a test would not be honored" hmm.

Actually I recall the real fix commit: `pytest-dev/pytest` commit "fix: dynamically added xfail markers are now honored" — the change was in `pytest_runtest_makereport` to call `evaluate_xfail_marks(item)` again instead of using the stored value. Let me look at the code in the repo to be sure.

Let me explore.

This is the pytest repo at 6.0.0rc1-ish. The issue is pytest issue #7486: "Dynamically adding xfail marker in test no longer ignores failure". The fix was in src/_pytest/skipping.py — the xfail evaluation was moved to setup, and it checked `rep_call` etc. The actual fix (PR #7486 fix was commit "skipping: fix dynamically adding xfail marker" ... let me recall.

The real fix: pytest issue #7486. The fix was in PR #7486? Actually the fix commit is https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/pull/7486 — "fix dynamically adding xfail". Let me recall the code.

In pytest 6.0.0rc1, skipping.py had:

```python
@pytest.hookimpl(hookwrapper=True)
def pytest_runtest_makereport(item: Item, call: CallInfo[None]):
    outcome = yield
    rep = outcome.get_result()
    xfailed = item._store.get(xfailed_key, False)
    if xfailed:
        ...
```

and in pytest_runtest_setup:

```python
def pytest_runtest_setup(item):
    ...
    evaluate_xfail_marks(item)
```

The bug: in 6.0, xfail markers were evaluated at setup time only (stored in item._store), so markers added during the test call (e.g., in a fixture or in the test itself via request.node.add_marker) were not seen. The fix (PR #7486, commit 8f5b771c) changed pytest_runtest_makereport to re-evaluate xfail marks at call time.

No — 6.2.5 was the last 6.2.x, released Oct 2021... Let me just check what the fix looks like: set lineno/col_offset on the alias nodes. Something like:

def _make_alias(name, asname, lineno, col_offset):

- `pytest_runtest_call`: after `yield`, re-evaluate xfail marks if none are stored — so markers added during the run are honored by the reporting hook.
